title: The determinism guarantee is broken by default: the CLI leaks the checkout directory name into output
evidence: The business promise is "output is byte-identical for the same sources and options on any machine" and the model crate's contract says "no ambient data... no absolute paths" (`crates/sealmap-model/src/lib.rs:33`-`34`). But the CLI, when `--name` is not given, names the codebase after the canonicalised checkout directory (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:393`, `main.rs:419`-`424`), and that name reaches the index and overview. CI's determinism checks pin `--name sealmap` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:29`, `ci.yml:33`-`34`), so the tests cannot detect the default path's nondeterminism.
failure: Two agents or two machines clone the same tree into differently named directories and run `sealmap generate` with default flags; the index/overview bytes differ. Downstream caching by content hash misses or, worse, a diff flags "changes" that are only directory names, sending reviewers a false review pack; seal comparisons made under different names also diverge (`stale --since` reads the older tree under the current tree's name).
confidence: high

title: The shipped seal gate misses roughly one in four real changes, yet remains a published command whose pass state reads as "current"
evidence: The CLI ships `resolve`, `stale`, `seal-check`, `verify`, `seal sign` (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:45`-`65`, published at 0.2.1, `Cargo.toml:6`), and the lifecycle marks a topic `Holds` when "ids resolve, sig and body match". The measured fact: "the per-symbol rule caught 0.76 of real staleness (`README.md:81`-`85`)" and "every staleness rule finer than per-file lost real changes" — which is why the surface was frozen (`docs/DESIGN.md:3`-`41`).
failure: An adopter runs `sealmap verify` as a staleness gate; `Holds` is read as "diagram is current", but ~24% of real code changes pass through uncited bodies. Agents consume stale diagrams believed verified. The defect is silent by construction — a miss produces a green gate.
confidence: high
marked_by_authors: no (disclosed as an evidence-programme outcome, not flagged as a defect in the shipped surface)

title: The declared MSRV is false for every downstream consumer: published crates can pull `ignore` 0.4.30, which needs Rust 1.88
evidence: The workspace declares `rust-version 1.85` (`Cargo.toml:8`) and the business section promises "builds on a stated, tested minimum Rust (1.85)". The msrv job passes only because `Cargo.lock` pins `ignore` 0.4.29 (`Cargo.lock:290`) under `--locked` (`ci.yml:46`); the requirement is deliberately left at `0.4.23` (`Cargo.toml:35`), and 0.4.30 declares no `rust-version`, so "the resolver cannot avoid it" and it needs Rust 1.88 (`Cargo.toml:32`-`33`). A published crate ships without the lockfile.
failure: Any downstream project on Rust 1.85 depending on the published crates resolves `ignore` 0.4.30 and fails to build. The remedy is a manual pin each consumer must discover from a comment (`Cargo.toml:32`-`34`). The core adoption promise fails exactly for the audience it was made to.
confidence: high
marked_by_authors: yes (Tension "MSRV vs dependency" and a Debt note)

title: "No environment" determinism likely has a second hole: the loader honours ignore files, which may reach outside the source tree
evidence: The contract forbids ambient input (`crates/sealmap-model/src/lib.rs:33`), but the model crate depends on `ignore` because "the model crate's loader honours ignore files" (`crates/sealmap-model/Cargo.toml:21`) — with no stated scope limit. The `ignore` crate's default walker also reads parent-directory and user-global exclude files; whether sealmap disables that is not stated anywhere in the material.
failure: The same tree generates a different model on two machines whose global gitignore/excludes differ (or when cloned at different depths) — files silently vanish from the model, diagrams lose coverage, and the divergence is invisible because each machine is self-consistent. This would defeat the cache/diff promise independently of F-01.
confidence: medium, inferred — the dependency and its purpose are stated; the default-scope behaviour is external knowledge. Verify whether the walker disables parents/global excludes.

title: Nothing in CI verifies the corpus against the code at HEAD, and the one tool that could fails on this repository today
evidence: "No job runs `sealmap verify`, and none is planned" (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:9`-`84`, DEL-01.1); the diagrams job checks citations only "at its topic's stamp" (`ci.yml:78`), i.e. historically. When run at `ae478d9`, `verify` exits 1 on MER-02 (`crates/sealmap-corpus/src/seal/check.rs:390`) and treats fifteen of sixteen topics as "coverage only, never a failure" (`check.rs:391`-`392`).
failure: Code is edited at HEAD; `path:line` citations and diagrams rot. No CI signal exists (the replacement — weekly per-file flags triaged by a model — is an out-of-band process, `README.md:367`-`378`). Agents follow citations into wrong lines of code. Turning `verify` on later requires content fixes first (MER-02) plus migrating fifteen topics, so the gate cannot be adopted incrementally without a dedicated effort.
confidence: high
marked_by_authors: no (presented as a closed decision, step 6, `docs/DESIGN.md:26`-`30`)

title: The seal lock's reviewer field is unenforced self-attestation, and the enforcement script will never exist
evidence: The design left reviewer family, evidence and signatures to a skill script `seal-gate.mjs` (`docs/DESIGN.md:165`-`166`). DEL-02.4 states the consequence plainly: "that script will not be written, so `seal sign` records whatever reviewer string it is given and nothing enforces the cross-family rule."
failure: A seal lock is usable as evidence that a second, different-family reviewer saw the change. In practice any string is accepted: a developer or agent self-seals without cross-family review and the lock looks compliant. If seals are relied on as an audit trail of review, the trail is forgeable with no detection mechanism anywhere in the shipped code.
confidence: high

title: Review packs are not reproducible records: `--diff` compares a revision to the dirty working tree, not two named trees
evidence: The business section calls the pack "one bounded, reproducible file". DEL-02.3 records that `pack` "was built to its own flags rather than the planned ones: `--diff REV` against the working tree instead of two named trees" (`docs/DESIGN.md:203`, `docs/DESIGN.md:213`-`222`).
failure: A pack's contents depend on uncommitted local state. Once the working tree changes, the exact artifact a reviewer saw cannot be regenerated from git history; two runs on two machines with different dirty states produce different packs (compounded by F-01 if `--name` is unset). The review record has no custody — you cannot later prove what was reviewed.
confidence: medium — the flag semantics are stated; the irreproducibility follows from them

title: The seal gate fails open: a topic silently loses all enforcement when its citations stop being recognised
evidence: Topics "with no seal and no citation: coverage only, never a failure" (`crates/sealmap-corpus/src/seal/check.rs:391`-`392`). The design intended this so a corpus "could not migrate one topic at a time" (`docs/DESIGN.md:161`-`163`) — but the same rule means a topic that had citations and loses them (prose reformatting, span styling, id grammar drift) exits enforcement with no signal of any kind.

confidence: high on the stated semantics; the prose-loss path is inferred from MER-02 showing prose parsing is the citation mechanism

evidence: "Nothing generated is committed any more, so the gate is that two generations agree byte for byte... not that a committed copy matches" (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:24`-`25`); the committed corpus and its drift gate were "retired in step 3" (DEL-01 history).
